thread:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — thinking through a simple, operator-friendly 'keystone handoff' for airgapped upgrades. sketch: write an activation anchor (keystone) to the local ledger when a node finishes apply; operator watches for N anchors, then issues a promotion that flips a single activation bit. avoids global locks. thoughts?

aj: high level lgtm. main worry is partial-apply corruption if node crashes between writing keystone and flipping activation. how do we ensure replay/resume won't double-apply or leave inconsistent state? :thinking:

devon: two ideas: 1) three-phase marker: PREPARE (download + verify), COMMIT_CANDIDATE (apply steps + write keystone w/ digest), FINALIZE (operator promotion flips activated=true). the node refuses to move to FINALIZE without keystone digest match.

maria: yep. the keystone would include apply-hash + list of components applied. operator promotion only checks keystone consensus (e.g. 3-of-5) and then issues a cluster-wide 'finalize anchor'. nodes seeing finalize compare anchors and finalize if digest matches.

aj: ok. what about rollbacks and partial-rollforward? if a later package is promoted but some nodes lag, do we allow staggered activation?

sam: we should allow staggered activation within a bounded window. operator can set a promotion-window TTL and a safety cutoff. nodes that lag beyond cutoff must auto-rollback to last activated snapshot or require manual intervention. keep auto-recovery conservative.

devon: mechanism sketch (pseudo):
```
# node on apply completion
write_local_keystone({digest: D, components: [...], version: V})
# operator: wait for quorum of keystones (same D)
promote_keystone(D, window=15m)
# nodes: on seeing promote(D) -> if local_keystone.digest == D -> set activated=true
# else -> if has older activated snapshot -> stay on old; report mismatch
```

maria: +1. also recommend publishing a per-node attestation blob (signed by node key) when writing keystone so operator can validate nodes didn't lie about components. this helps when using physical media or human-curated transport.

aj: attestation makes sense. one more nit: what about idempotency when apply is retried? we need deterministic apply ordering and a compact change log so replay is safe. maybe require apply ops be commutative or guard them with check-and-set using component-hashes.

devon: agree. implement a compact apply-log file that's append-only and checkpointed. replay checks the last logged op before reapplying. treat apply as idempotent by skipping ops with matching op-id.

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered: new draft rfc uploaded -> /rfc/keystone-handoff-2026.md :thumbsup:

sam: UX suggestions for operator console: show 'quorum heatmap' (which nodes have keystone D), offer a one-click promote with safety checks, and an automated dry-run mode that simulates finalize without flipping activation. small teams can use auto-promote but big customers prefer manual gating.

maria: this is great — I'll fold the three-phase markers, attestations, and the promote-window TTL into the follow-up RFC. will add a short sequence diagram and operator CLI examples (promote with --dry-run).

aj: sounds good. pls add a paragraph on observability: expose per-node keystone digest, last-apply-op-id, and a reconcile endpoint so console can force re-eval.

maria: will do. thanks all :rocket:
